title: 第 34 課｜剛體的運動方程：力與力矩｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
剛體有六個自由度，所以運動方程一共需要六條，而它們可以寫成兩個向量的時間導數。第一條由每個質點的動量變化率加總得到：總動量 P = μV，於是 dP/dt = F。這裡的 F 只包含外力，因為質點之間的內力永遠成對出現、大小相等方向相反，加起來自動抵消。若剛體處在外場中，把勢能對質心座標微分就得到這個力，F = − ∂U/∂R；理由是把整個物體平移 δR 時每一點都改變同樣的量，所以 δU = − F · δR。第二條方程給角動量的變化率：取一個此刻質心靜止的參考系，位置向量的導數與動量平行、那個叉積為零，只剩 K = Σ r × f，於是 dM/dt = K。力矩和角動量一樣依賴原點的選擇：把原點移動 a，新的力矩滿足 K = K′ + a × F。由此立刻看出，當總力為零時力矩與原點無關，這時物體受到的是一個力偶，它不推動質心、只讓物體轉動。這兩條方程也可以直接從拉格朗日量得到：∂L/∂Ωᵢ = Mᵢ，而把物體轉過一個無限小角度可得 K = − ∂U/∂φ。最後一個漂亮的結果是：若總力與總力矩互相垂直，一定能找到位移使新原點的力矩為零，因此 K = a × F；滿足條件的點構成一整條直線，所有作用力都可以化成沿著這條直線作用的單一個力。均勻場正是這種情形：每個質點受力 f = eE，總力 F = E Σe，總力矩 K = r₀ × F，其中 r₀ = Σ e r / Σ e 是用係數加權平均出來的點。在均勻重力場裡係數就是質量，這個點正好是質心，這也是為什麼重力可以畫成質心上的一支箭頭。影片以翻滾飛行的剛體、等勢面上的梯度力、可滑動原點的即時力矩長條圖、指南針式的 U(φ) 曲線、可滑動的作用線與加權平均的槓桿平衡動畫呈現。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 34 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 34 | The Equations of Motion of a Rigid Body: Force and Torque | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
A rigid body has six degrees of freedom, so its equations of motion must be six in all, and they can be written as the time derivatives of two vectors. The first follows from summing the momentum change over every particle: the total momentum is P = μV, so dP/dt = F. Only external forces enter F, because the internal ones come in equal and opposite pairs and cancel. In an external field this force is the derivative of the potential energy with respect to the centre-of-mass coordinates, F = − ∂U/∂R, since translating the whole body by δR shifts every point equally and gives δU = − F · δR. The second equation gives the rate of change of the angular momentum. Working in a frame where the centre of mass is momentarily at rest, each position vector's derivative is parallel to the momentum, so that cross product drops out and only K = Σ r × f survives, giving dM/dt = K. Torque, like angular momentum, depends on the origin: moving it by a displacement a gives K = K′ + a × F. One special case follows at once — when the total force vanishes the torque no longer depends on the origin, and the body is acted on by a couple, which does not push the centre of mass but only makes it turn. Both equations also follow from the Lagrangian: ∂L/∂Ωᵢ = Mᵢ, and rotating the body through an infinitesimal angle gives K = − ∂U/∂φ. Finally, if the total force and torque are perpendicular, some displacement always makes the torque about the new origin vanish, so K = a × F; the points that work form a whole straight line, and all the applied forces reduce to a single force acting along it. A uniform field is exactly this case: each particle feels f = eE, the total force is F = E Σe, and the total torque is K = r₀ × F with r₀ = Σ e r / Σ e, the weighted average point. In a uniform gravitational field the coefficient is the mass and that point is the centre of mass, which is why weight can be drawn as one arrow there. Animated with a tumbling body on a parabolic flight, the gradient force on equipotential curves, a live torque bar readout as the origin slides, a compass needle beside its U(φ) curve, a sliding line of action, and a balance beam for the weighted average.

Lesson 34 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
